newsitem.title: DUBAI: Abu Dhabi plans to set up petrochemical firm.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi plans to set up petrochemical firm.

text.p: Abu Dhabi has approved the creation of a one billion UAE dirhams ($272 million) firm to produce oil derivatives and petrochemicals, the UAE English-language Khaleej Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
"The Government of Abu Dhabi will own 51 percent of the company's shares and the rest will be held by private firms and businessmen," an unnamed source told the paper.
Foreign investment in the firm, which would produce plastics and textiles, was being considered, the source added.
The new company, which would be based at the planned Saadiyat Duty Free Zone in Abu Dhabi, would work jointly with the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC).

ADNOC committed itself to the petrochemical business in June when its signed a $1 billion-plus joint-venture deal with Norwegian-Finnish firm Borealis to build a 450,000 tonnes a year polyethylene plant in the Gulf emirate.
No time frame was given for the setting up the new firm which would be administered by the Abu Dhabi state-run General Industry Corporation, the paper said.
Abu Dhabi is planning to build a $3 billion trade zone on the Gulf island of Saadiyat, east of Abu Dhabi city over the next three to four years.
Abu Dhabi's move into petrochemicals was prompted by the need to diversify its oil-dominated economy.
